title: Lossy-stream JSON recovery and escape semantics for truncated streams
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When streaming model responses that must be parsed as structured JSON and/or include tool/function call handoffs, network or token limits can truncate the stream mid-JSON token or mid-escape sequence. Current retry and resume behavior is brittle: clients often receive invalid JSON (broken escape sequences, half-objects) which leads to spurious failures, inconsistent tool invocations, or duplicate tool calls after retries.

Goal: Define and implement a robust server+client protocol and runtime handling that allows graceful detection of lossy/truncated structured streams, safe retries with idempotent tool-call resumes, and an escape/rewrite strategy that preserves semantic intent while minimizing downstream parsing errors and customer-facing failures.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits deterministic fragment headers for stream checkpoints (stream-id, fragment-seq, fragment-checksum) before first user-facing JSON token.

Client and server agree on a compact escape map for partial-escape sequences; partial escapes are canonically encoded as 'ESC-HEX' tokens in the fragment header so parsers can recover deterministically.

On truncation detection, clients should be able to request resume from the last successful fragment-seq; server accepts resume token and replays idempotent suffix or returns a canonical 'incomplete' manifest when replay is impossible.

Tool/function calls are only emitted with a server-signed call-manifest including an idempotency-key and pre-call checksum; retries do not produce additional side effects unless the idempotency-key is explicitly unacknowledged.

End-to-end integration tests demonstrating recovery for: (a) mid-string unicode escape truncation, (b) truncation inside nested arrays/objects, (c) truncation combined with streaming toolcall metadata interleaving.
Performance regression <5% at p95 latency for typical streaming workloads after changes to framing/headers and resume flow.
Docs and SDK example implemented for Node/Python showing client resume dance and server manifest verification.
Console traces surface stream-fragment events and resume outcomes for debugging (trace spans + fragment metadata visible in per-request view).
technical_notes: We must avoid expensive per-token cryptography; use an incremental CRC32C or farmhash64 as fragment-checksum for speed and deterministic collision behavior.
Checkpoint header should be <= 128 bytes to avoid significant payload overhead; include minimal fields: version, stream-id, fragment-seq, checksum, open-escape-bitmask.

Open-escape-bitmask encodes whether the fragment ends in the middle of an escape sequence or inside an open string/object. This allows client parsers to do guided repair instead of blind concatenation.

Server-side streaming pipeline will introduce a small marshalling step to prepend fragment headers and compute checksums before sending; benchmark required across models and sequence length distributions.

Toolcall manifests: include fields (call-id, idempotency-key, pre-state-checksum, expected-output-shape). The runtime must garble-proof manifest signing with the platform key so clients can verify authenticity without contacting external services.
Backpressure: if fragment generation is delayed, prefer emitting a lightweight heartbeat header with last-fragment-seq to keep clients aligned rather than producing partial JSON.
Compatibility: fall back to old behavior when client indicates 'compat-mode=v1' in Accept header. New mode 'compat-mode=v2' enables fragment headers and deterministic resume semantics.
Security: avoid leaking internal model state in headers. stream-id must be an opaque UUID with TTL; checksums must be non-reversible.
For on-prem/private deployments, feature gate via runtime flag 'stream_fragmenting=on' so customers can opt-in after testing.
proposed_solution: Phase 1 (spec + opt-in): Define wire-level fragment header spec and escape map; implement producer-side header prepending in runtime; add runtime flag + SDK opt-in examples.

Phase 2 (resume logic): Implement server resume endpoint /v1/streams/:id/resume accepting last known fragment-seq + client parser state snapshot and returning replayed suffix or canonical 'incomplete' manifest.
Phase 3 (toolcall idempotency): Add call-manifest signing and idempotency enforcement in the tool router; ensure calls without completed manifest are flagged and never executed twice.
Phase 4 (rollout + metrics): Enable cross-region canary, collect p95 latency, resume-success-rate, duplicate-call incidents, and parsing-error rates; iterate on header size and heartbeat cadence.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Spec review with product, SDK, security, and docs. Publish design doc (Drive) and RFC.
Week 2: Implement lightweight header glue in staging runtime; expose opt-in flag. Merge feature branch behind feature flag.
Week 3: SDK patch for Node/Python with resume helper utilities and examples; integration tests added to CI.
Week 4: Internal canary for <1% traffic with new header; monitor errors and latency.
Week 5: Expand to 20% with automated rollback if duplicate-call rate increases >0.1% or parsing-error reduction <50%.
Week 6: Full rollout and docs promotion; add Console fragments trace UI and dashboard tile.
test_plan: Unit: fragment header encoder/decoder, open-escape-bitmask derivation, checksum correctness against golden vectors.
Integration: simulate TCP truncation at random offsets across token boundaries for 100k synthetic streams; assert resume success or canonical incomplete-manifest return in >= 99.5% of cases.
Toolcall: instrument a fake tool that records invocations and verify idempotent behavior for repeated resumes using same idempotency-key.
E2E: SDK-driven smoke tests replicating user flows that chain structured JSON -> toolcall -> structured JSON with intentional truncation and timed retries.
Performance: benchmark p50/p95/p99 latency before/after with stress tests (batching disabled/enabled) to ensure <5% regression at p95.
Chaos: restart streaming runtime mid-fragment and validate resume semantics and no double-execution of side-effecting toolcalls.
